mockLlm.purpose: Reference execution must not depend on a paid model endpoint (Phase 1B). The mock is CopilotKit's own, so fixture-backed reference behavior stays reference-attributable rather than introducing a foreign test double.
mockLlm.warning: Never use npx for these names: aimock@0.2.9 and llmock@3.3.6 are unrelated packages on npm.

programmaticServing.why: The recorded d4 chain's tool-result legs are unreachable through the flag-driven llmock bin: the pristine example sets a2ui={{ catalog }} unconditionally (layout.tsx:48), so the sdk-js LangGraph middleware appends an 'App Context:' developer message to every model request (observed LAST on the wire, twice in multi-tool turns), while llmock's toolCallId rule requires the final message to be role:'tool' (dist/router.js:243-244). No showcase test covers this chain, which is why the incompatibility shipped.
programmaticServing.mechanism: reference/aimock-server.mjs runs the pinned library's own LLMock class programmatically with the requestTransform server option (server.js:384 feeds it into matchFixtureDiagnostic) that drops 'App Context:' developer/system messages for MATCHING only; the reference app stays byte-identical to the pin and the injector archives every request unaltered under logs/raw/.
programmaticServing.sideEffects: Supplying requestTransform flips llmock to useExactMatch (router.js:193), so journey prompts must equal fixture match.userMessage byte-for-byte. chunkSize 9999 is set programmatically (fixture streams emoji; UTF-16 default 20 splits surrogate pairs).
proven: Leg-by-leg replay of the archived jc6 bodies against the transformed server: entry 200, enable_app_mode tool-result -> manage_todos 200, manage_todos tool-result -> 'Done - added three todos' 200, all with the trailing App Context message present
Full in-app chain under Playwright: 16 hits / 0 misses across the J-C session (jc9), each leg streaming through the reference agent
non-streaming chat completion returns the fixture completion
stream:true emits well-formed SSE deltas followed by [DONE]
all of the above with OPENAI_API_KEY unset
the canonical starter's own model traffic matched fixtures: injector tally moved hit=3 -> hit=4 during a scripted UI turn, with 'HIT POST /v1/chat/completions -> 200' and miss=0

fixtureCoverageFindings.columns: showcase/aimock holds 873 fixture files across 21 agent columns; d6/langgraph-typescript alone carries 43 shared-state, chat, GenUI, HITL, interrupt, A2UI, MCP and thread fixtures
fixtureCoverageFindings.matchingModel: aimock selects on match.userMessage (substring) plus match.context; tool-result follow-ups select on match.toolCallId; turnIndex and hasToolResult further gate some fixtures
fixtureCoverageFindings.sharedStateFixturesTargetAnotherSurface: shared-state-read-write declares a set_notes tool call whose notes render into the showcase app's Preferences/Agent Scratch Pad panels. The canonical starter's canvas is a todo column bound to agent.state.todos, and no fixture anywhere in the tree emits a write_todos/manage_todos call. The agent-to-canvas state write therefore cannot be mock-driven on the canonical starter; it needs the showcase app or a recorded fixture
fixtureCoverageFindings.recallFixturesAreScripted: The recall fixtures (for example favorite color -> 'Your favorite color is blue - I noted it earlier.') match on the user message alone, so a rendered recall reply proves the mock served a fixture, not that the agent read shared state. The claim-bearing observable is the outbound model request, which the context injector now logs to a sidecar with the last user message, a state-field indicator and requested markers
fixtureCoverageFindings.uncovered: one MISS was logged for a prompt authored by the capture rather than taken from a fixture; after captures switched to fixture-declared prompts the miss count stayed 0

executionStatus.note: The canonical starter executes headlessly against the pinned mock with no paid endpoint. GREEN (J-A, J-C, J-E, J-F, J-H, J-J) with zero run-scoped misses on every run report. UNCOVERED (J-D, J-G, J-K): each has a run report carrying outcome UNCOVERED with the scenario, the reason, the fixture that exists, why it is not reachable on this surface, and its evidence class - recorded rather than synthesized. J-J's post flow is OBSERVED_ABSENT: the capture ran and the observed absence, with its wire metric, is the evidence. Prior Vitest results stand: 23/23 official React-core fixture tests.
executionStatus.pendingBlocker: No blocker for reference capture: every canonical journey now has a run report with an explicit outcome. The pinned Turbopack/CSS defect fires on boot, mid-session and on mid-run reload; harness.mjs heal cold-restarts the UI and requires status<500, and `heal` recovers without disturbing the mock/agent. Remaining work is the unbuilt Cognate journeys (R2) and the parity artifacts (diffs/, parity-report, primitive-provenance), not reference execution.

journeyCoverage.harness: reference/harness.mjs — boot | heal | run <journey> | status | shots | down
journeyCoverage.exitSemantics: run exits 0 for GREEN and for a RECORDED UNCOVERED gap (the record is the evidence), 1 only for FAILED. Read `outcome`, never the code alone, to separate proven from declared-missing.

referenceSurfaceFacts: The threads drawer (copilotkit-threads-drawer, Lit, OPEN shadow root) paints as a persistent LEFT SIDEBAR on desktop; page.tsx notes the header launcher it registers exists only on mobile, where the drawer is off-canvas. There is no [aria-label] in light DOM at all - a '[aria-label=Open threads]' launcher selector finds nothing on this surface.

Threads drawer internals are addressable through shadow-piercing CSS: new thread = copilotkit-threads-drawer [part="new-thread-button"], rows = li[data-thread-id] with the active row carrying .active. Thread NAMES are model-generated, so a row is identified by its data-thread-id, never by its text.

J-E turn 1 renders the component on the tool CALL, before the tool result that carries the reply marker - the pending state is only observable between those two, which is why journeys accept an intermediate observation (turn.mid) rather than waiting on the terminal marker alone.

The pinned Turbopack defect also fires on mid-run page reload, not only at boot: a reload recompiles globals.css, emits the invalid escape, and serves a Next build-error overlay. harness.mjs heal (cold-restart of .next, status<500 required) absorbs it; `heal` is exposed as its own command so a broken UI can be recovered without `boot` taking down a healthy mock/agent.
